$comment: The chat router's labeled route set (#9925): realistic first messages across the 12 routes of docs/coder/design/2026-09-28-chat-router.md, each with the route, the prepared answer (or null), other acceptable answers, the tier, the risk, and the CLI group a correct router picks.

split is fixed: a row is held_out when the first four bytes of SHA-256(id), as a big-endian integer, modulo 100 are below 30. Held-out rows are never used to pick thresholds or tune `when` text; the test in crates/coder/src/router_eval.rs recomputes it.
Secrets in `refuse` rows are fake placeholders, never real keys.

An eval.run row's tool is the catalog tool its message names, or null when it names none (the router then offers the default tool, Project map); the live eval checks the start_eval offer against it (#9943).

Relabeled 2026-09-28 against the landed bank, uniformly across splits: meta.data_retention rows also accept meta.privacy, whose text says the worker keeps no message text, and meta.team rows also accept meta.who, whose `when` covers who built us. The bank has neither meta.data_retention nor meta.team.

chat-router-v2 (#9936): the v1 rows unchanged, with the same ids and splits, plus rows for the six Gym and eval routes (gym.news, eval.run, eval.author, eval.check, eval.result, eval.credit) and near misses between them and their neighbors (product.kb definitions, unit tests in the user's own repository, the XP command). Tier `gym` is a reply decided from the Gym's verified records; `author` is a step of the authoring interview.

chat-router-v3 (#9960): the v2 rows unchanged, with the same ids and splits, plus rows for the capability.missing route (a request that calls for a capability none of the admitted ones covers: booking, email, calendars, sites, devices, live data) and near misses that an admitted capability answers (questions about what we can do, work Coder does with a named tool, commands, the wallet, the account, the Gym, and making a capability). A capability.missing row's answer is capability.missing, or capability.missing_near when the reading names a close admitted capability. Tier `canned` for these is the bank's missing-capability line with its card.

chat-router-v4 (#10058): the v3 rows unchanged, with the same ids and splits, plus rows for the presentation.open route (asking to open, show, or present one of our decks, including decks we do not have) and near misses (writing or advice about talks and slides, opening another site or app, the deck code in our repository, and slides in the user's own project). A presentation.open row's answer is presentation.elsewhere, the line the set's default phone context gets; on the desktop the same reading serves presentation.open with its offer, or the presentation.unknown refusal.

#10073 (2026-09-30): the v4 rows unchanged, plus rows for an explicit request to delegate to Coder or run it now, including a trial or test delegation with no task named (work.dispatch, dispatch.stem), from the owner's chat "who are you", "who can you delegate to", "do a test delegation now", and near misses: asking whom or how we delegate (meta), testing a Gym tool on Coder (eval.run), and where delegation is implemented (codebase.kb). Tagged `delegation`.

#10076: rows tagged `engine`. work.dispatch rows name the coding engine the person asks for (`engine`: codex, claude_code, grok_build, opencode, devin), or null for none; every other work.dispatch row asks for none. Near misses name an engine only as a subject (asking a model in chat, comparing engines, where the adapter lives) and are not dispatches.

#10085 (2026-10-01): rows tagged `map`: asking to see how we route or are put together, our routes, members, plugins, and gaps (meta, answer meta.map, the line the set's default phone context gets; the desktop app's turns get meta.map.desktop with the routes.map open_screen offer), and near misses: what Jev is, what we can do, opening a deck, mapping the user's own repository, a map of the world, where the rubric lives in the code, making a plugin, and how network routers work.

#10094 (2026-10-01): rows tagged `coder_followup`: a follow-up in a chat whose Coder run ended, after the dispatch reply and the fixed line the worker puts before the latest message when the request's context.coder_run says the run ended (coder::router::CoderRun::marker; the run's own words never reach Jev). A question about what the run did, changed, or ran, or why it chose an engine, is answered in chat (general, tier model, from the run's result in the model's instructions); more work on it continues Coder as its next turn (work.dispatch). Near misses after a run take their own routes (a concept question, who we are, which computers are online, thanks, what Coder is, whether we write code).

#10099 (2026-10-01): rows tagged `essays`: questions about our two essays, Test-Time Capabilities and The Return of the General Agent, and the ideas in them (our thesis on general agents, test-time capabilities, capability claims, typed decision models), answered from product notes (product.kb), and near misses: concept questions not about our essays (general) and where the code implements something (codebase.kb). All in the tune split, so the published held-out record stays within NIP-EVAL's 256 cases.

#10102 (2026-10-01): more rows tagged `essays`: asking to summarize, give an overview of, explain, or compare our essays ("the essays", "both essays", "your essays", one essay by its subject), answered from the essays' product notes (product.kb), the #10099 gap "what makes a claim externally validated?", and near misses: summarizing a README, a file, or an essay in the user's own repository or computer (work.dispatch), and someone else's essay or writing help (general). And rows tagged `map`: asking to open or show the route map or the plugin map (meta, meta.map; meta.map.desktop on the desktop), with "try the project map plugin on coder" (eval.run, Project map) as a near miss. All in the tune split.

#10157 (2026-10-02): rows tagged `standing`: asking for something to keep happening on its own on the user's computer (a background rule: keep free space above a level, prune worktrees on a schedule, warn about low disk, tell them when a Coder run fails or ends, keep a checkout up to date every morning) or changing, pausing, resuming, or removing one (standing.rule). All in the tune split, so the held-out partition stays at NIP-EVAL's 256 cases; the live eval reads them with ROUTER_EVAL_ROWS=standing ROUTER_EVAL_SPLIT=all. Labeled for the set's default phone context, where the line says rules are set up on the computer (standing.elsewhere; a terminal serves standing.rule and compiles the rule there). Near misses tagged `near-miss`: doing it once now (work.dispatch), a one-time reminder or anything outside the computer such as email (capability.missing), how scheduling works in general (general), how background rules work (product.kb), and listing rules or their log (cli, background).
